SOCIAL STUDIES
RELIGION AND NATIONAL VALUES

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Religion is the belief, faith and worship in the existence of God.
Religion is also the mode of worshipping God. The major religion in Nigeria are Christianity, Islam and Traditional religions.
CHRISTIAN MODE OF WORSHIP
Christianity is one the religions practised in Nigeria. The believers worship God in the name of His begotten son - Jesus Christ.
Christians worship in the church every Sunday and some other days of week depending on their church’s activities.
Some materials which Christians use for worship are the Holy Bible, the rosary, hymn books, water and olive oil.
Christians celebrate the birth (Christmas), the death (Good Friday), resurrection (Easter Sunday) and ascension (Easter Monday) of our Lord, Jesus Christ.
A man is expected to marry one wife. Christians sometimes go on pilgrimage to Jerusalem. Christianity was brought into Nigeria from Western countries.
LESSON 2 - MUSLIMS MODE OF WORSHIP
Islam is also one of the religions practiced in Nigeria. The Islamic faithfuls or followers of Islam are called Muslims. Islam is a religion introduced by Prophet Muhammad. The Holy Book of the Muslim is called the Quran (Koran).
The Muslims worship in the Mosque every Friday and prayed five times a day. They use a string of beads for prayers. They worship in a building called a mosque.
Muslims go on pilgrimage to Mecca. Muslims fast for thirty days during Ramadan. A Muslim man is allowed to marry up to four wives if he can love them equally.
Like Christianity, Islam was also brought into Nigerian from other countries.
LESSON 3 - AFRICAN TRADITION MODE OF WORSHIP
African Traditional Religion is an indigenous religion.
The religion practices are vary from one community to another. This religion is parts of our culture. It is a way of worshipping God, traditionally.
They worship God through lesser gods and goddess in objects. These gods and goddesses are regarded as servants of God.
For Examples of such gods and goddesses in Nigeria include:
1. Amadioha, the god of thunder among the Igbo.
2. Ogun, the god of iron among the Yoruba.
3. Olokun, the water goddess among the Edo.
Some of the materials used are palm oil, cowries, kola nuts, goats, native chalk and pieces of white cloth.
The priest tells the worshippers what to do and on which days to worship.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guides the pupils to discuss the meaning of religion.
Pupil’s Activities - Discuss the meaning of religion.
3. Lets them mention different types of religion in Nigeria.
Pupil’s Activities - Mention the major religion in Nigeria.
4. Asks the pupils to mention each religion place of worship and materials used in worship.
Pupil’s Activities - Mention each religion place of worship and materials used in worship.
5. Summary the key points on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher write.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

topics.content:
RELATIONSHIP AMONG FAMILY MEMBERS: FAMILY TREE, FAMILY RELATIONSHIPS AND BENEFITS OF THE FAMILY
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 2
THEME - FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY
PREVIOUS LESSON - Living in the Family: Meaning and Types of Family, Members of Nuclear and Extended Family, and Importance of the Family | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 1 Social Studies
TOPIC - RELATIONSHIP AMONG FAMILY MEMBERS
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Family Tree and Drawing a Simple Family Tree
3. Meaning and Importance of Family Relationship
4. Benefits of Family
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of a family tree.
2. Explain the meaning of family relationship.
3. Identify the different relationships among family members.
4. Draw and label a simple family tree.
5. State at least five benefits of the family.
6. Explain the importance of maintaining good relationships among family members.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the meaning of family, the types of family, and the members of nuclear and extended families.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing the family tree, explaining family relationships, and discussing the benefits of the family.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Family tree chart
2. Pictures of nuclear and extended families
3. Flashcards showing family members (father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, uncle, aunt, cousin, brother, sister)
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every family has different members who are connected in different ways. Some people are our parents, others are our grandparents, brothers, sisters, uncles, aunts, or cousins. A family tree helps us understand how these family members are related to one another.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of a family tree, understand family relationships, and explain the benefits of the family in helping people live happily together.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF A FAMILY TREE
A family tree is a simple diagram or chart that shows the members of a family and how they are related to one another.
It helps us understand our family history and relationships.
MEANING OF FAMILY RELATIONSHIP
A family relationship is the connection or bond between members of a family through birth, marriage, or adoption.
Examples include the relationship between:
1. Parents and children
2. Brothers and sisters
3. Grandparents and grandchildren
4. Uncles, aunts, and cousins
COMMON FAMILY RELATIONSHIPS
1. Father - Male parent
2. Mother - Female parent
3. Son - Male child
4. Daughter - Female child
5. Brother - Male sibling
6. Sister - Female sibling
7. Grandfather - Father of one’s father or mother
8. Grandmother - Mother of one’s father or mother
9. Uncle - Brother of one’s father or mother
10. Aunt - Sister of one’s father or mother
11. Cousin - Child of one’s uncle or aunt
LESSON 2 - BENEFITS OF THE FAMILY
The family:
1. Provides love and care.
2. Provides food, clothing, and shelter.
3. Protects family members.
4. Teaches good morals and discipline.
5. Gives children education and guidance.
6. Encourages cooperation and unity.
7. Helps family members solve problems.
8. Preserves family traditions and culture.
9. Provides emotional support.
10. Teaches responsibility and respect.
IMPORTANCE OF KNOWING FAMILY RELATIONSHIPS
Knowing family relationships helps us to:
1. Respect family members.
2. Understand our family history.
3. Know our responsibilities.
4. Promote peace and unity.
5. Strengthen family love and cooperation.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. A family tree is a chart that shows ______.
A. different kinds of trees
B. the roads in a community
C. the subjects taught in school
D. family members and how they are related

A. grandfather
B. uncle
C. cousin
D. brother
3. Your mother’s sister is your ______.

B. aunt
C. daughter
D. cousin
4. The child of your uncle or aunt is your ______.
A. brother
B. nephew
C. cousin
D. grandfather

A. Destroying property
B. Causing quarrels
C. Encouraging bad behaviour
D. Providing love and care
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: aunt, love, family tree, guidance, grandfather,
6. A ______ shows how family members are related.
7. My father’s father is my ______.
8. My mother’s sister is my ______.
9. A good family provides ______ and care.
10. Parents give children good ______.
C. True or False
11. Brothers and sisters are different members of the same family. ______
12. A family tree helps us know our family relationships. ______
13. Families should always quarrel with one another. ______
14. Uncles and aunts are members of the extended family. ______
15. Families teach children bad morals. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B

17. Uncle - B. Child of an uncle or aunt
18. Cousin - C. Gives love, care, and protection
19. Brother - D. Brother of your father or mother
20. Family - E. Mother of your father or mother
ANSWER KEYS
1. D. family members and how they are related
2. A. grandfather
3. B. aunt
4. C. cousin
5. D. Providing love and care
6. family tree
7. grandfather
8. aunt
9. love
10. guidance
11. False
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. False

17. D. Brother of your father or mother

19. A. Male child of the same parents
20. C. Gives love, care, and protection
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that a family tree is a diagram or chart that shows the members of a family and how they are related to one another.
They also learned that family relationships describe the connection between family members, such as father, mother, son, daughter, brother, sister, grandfather, grandmother, uncle, aunt, and cousin.
Pupils identified different family relationships using a simple family tree and understood how each family member is connected to another.
Finally, pupils discussed the benefits of the family, including providing love, care, protection, food, clothing, shelter, guidance, education, emotional support, cooperation, and good moral values. They concluded that maintaining good relationships among family members promotes peace, unity, respect, and happy family living.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays a simple family tree chart and asks pupils to identify the people shown in it. The teacher then introduces the topic Relationship Among Family Members.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the family members and describe how they are related.
Step 2: Meaning of a Family Tree
The teacher explains that a family tree is a diagram or chart that shows family members and how they are related. Also, the teacher demonstrates how to read a simple family tree.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of a family tree and identify family members on the chart.
Step 3: Meaning of Family Relationship
The teacher explains that family relationship is the connection between family members through birth, marriage, or adoption.
Also, the teacher discusses common family relationships such as:
- Father
- Mother
- Son
- Daughter
- Brother
- Sister
- Grandfather
- Grandmother
- Uncle
- Aunt
- Cousin
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the relationships between different family members.
Step 4: Drawing a Simple Family Tree
The teacher draws a simple family tree on the board and labels each family member correctly. Also, the teacher explains how the family tree helps us understand family relationships.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils copy and label a simple family tree in their notebooks.
Step 5: Benefits of the Family
The teacher explains the benefits of the family, including:
- Providing love and care.
- Providing food, clothing, and shelter.
- Giving guidance and education.
- Protecting family members.
- Teaching good morals and discipline.
- Promoting unity and cooperation.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss how their families help them every day.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following tasks:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of a family tree.
- Group 2: Identify relationships among family members using a family tree.
- Group 3: Draw and label a simple family tree.
- Group 4: State the benefits of the family.
- Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, draw, identify, and present their group work.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of a family tree, family relationships, and the benefits of the family.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher asks oral and written questions and assesses pupils’ ability to identify family relationships and explain the benefits of the family.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions, identify family members correctly, and explain the importance of good family relationships.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of a family tree.
2. Explain the meaning of family relationship.
3. Identify the relationships among family members.
4. Draw and label a simple family tree.
5. State at least five benefits of the family.
6. Explain the importance of maintaining good relationships among family members.

LIVING IN THE FAMILY: MEANING AND TYPES OF FAMILY, MEMBERS OF NUCLEAR AND EXTENDED FAMILY AND IMPORTANCE OF FAMILY
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 1
THEME -  FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY
PREVIOUS LESSON -
TOPIC - FAMILY
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Types of Family
3. Members of Nuclear and Extended Family
4. Importance of the Family
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of a family.
2. Identify the types of family.
3. List the members of a nuclear family.
4. Identify the members of an extended family.
5. State the importance of the family.
6. Explain the responsibilities of family members.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have interacted with members of their families at home and have learned about living together, caring for one another, and showing respect to parents and elders.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by helping pupils understand the meaning, types, members, and importance of the family.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Charts showing a nuclear family and an extended family
2. Family photographs
3. Flashcards with names of family members
4. Family tree chart
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every child belongs to a family. A family is the first place where a child learns how to speak, behave, respect others, and perform simple responsibilities. Some families consist of only parents and their children, while others include grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, and other relatives.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of a family, the types of family, the members of nuclear and extended families, and the importance of the family in our lives.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF FAMILY
A family is a group of people who are related by birth, marriage, or adoption and live together or care for one another.
The family is the first social group a child belongs to and where good behaviour, values, and responsibilities are learned.
TYPES OF FAMILY
There are two main types of family:
1. Nuclear Family
A nuclear family is made up of:
- Father
- Mother
- Children
It is also called the immediate family.
2. Extended Family
An extended family includes the nuclear family and other relatives, such as:
- Grandfather
- Grandmother
- Uncles
- Aunts
- Cousins
- Nephews
- Nieces
- Other close relatives
LESSON 2 - MEMBERS OF A NUCLEAR FAMILY
The members of a nuclear family are:
1. Father - The male parent who provides, protects, guides, and cares for the family.
2. Mother - The female parent who cares for the home, nurtures, and supports the family.
3. Son(s) - The male child or male children of the family.
4. Daughter(s) - The female child or female children of the family.
MEMBERS OF AN EXTENDED FAMILY
The members of an extended family include:
1. Father - The male parent of the family who provides, protects, and guides the household.
2. Mother - The female parent who cares for the family and helps in the upbringing of the children.
3. Children - The sons and daughters who belong to the family.
4. Grandfather - The father of one’s father or mother.
5. Grandmother - The mother of one’s father or mother.
6. Uncle - The brother of one’s father or mother.
7. Aunt - The sister of one’s father or mother.
8. Cousins - The children of one’s uncles and aunts.
9. Nephews - The sons of one’s brother or sister.
10. Nieces - The daughters of one’s brother or sister.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF THE FAMILY
The family is important because it:
1. Provides love and care.
2. Provides food, clothing, and shelter.
3. Protects family members.
4. Teaches good morals and discipline.
5. Gives children education and guidance.
6. Promotes unity and cooperation.
7. Helps children develop good behaviour.
8. Preserves family traditions and culture.
RESPONSIBILITIES OF FAMILY MEMBERS
1. Father: Provides for and protects the family.
2. Mother: Cares for the home and children.
3. Children: Obey their parents, respect elders, study hard, and help with simple household chores.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. A family is a group of people who are related by _______.
A. language, tribe, or state
B. occupation, leadership, or servants
C. birth, marriage, or adoption
D. religion, Christianity, or Muslim

A. Nuclear family
B. Classroom family
C. Football family
D. Market family

6. A _______ is the first social group a child belongs to.
7. An _______ family includes grandparents, uncles, and aunts.
8. The female parent is the _______.
9. The family provides food, clothing, and _______.
10. The children of your uncles and aunts are your _______.
C. True or False
11. A nuclear family consists of father, mother, and friends. _______
12. Grandparents are members of an extended family. _______
13. The family teaches good morals and discipline. _______
14. A cousin is the brother of your father. _______
15. Family members should love and care for one another. _______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Father - A. Male parent
17. Mother - B. Female parent
18. Uncle - C. Child of your uncle or aunt
19. Cousin - D. Mother of your father or mother
20. Grandmother - E. Brother of your father or mother
ANSWER KEYS
1. C - Birth, marriage, or adoption
2. A - Nuclear family
3. B - Father, mother, and children
4. D - Uncle
5. D - Provides love, care, and protection
6. family

8. mother

17. B - Female parent

19. C - Child of your uncle or aunt
20. D - Mother of your father or mother
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that a family is a group of people who are related by birth, marriage, or adoption and who love, care for, and support one another.
Pupils identified the two main types of family, namely the nuclear family and the extended family. They learned that a nuclear family consists of father, mother, and children, while an extended family includes other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews, and nieces.
They also identified the members of both nuclear and extended families and discussed the roles and responsibilities of different family members.
Finally, pupils understood the importance of the family in providing love, care, protection, food, clothing, shelter, education, moral training, guidance, cooperation, and support. They concluded that the family is the first social group where children learn good behaviour, values, and responsibilities.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher displays pictures of a nuclear family and an extended family. The teacher asks pupils to identify the people in each picture and describe their relationship before introducing the topic Living in the Family.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the family members and describe how they are related.
Step 2: Meaning of Family - The teacher explains that a family is a group of people who are related by birth, marriage, or adoption and who love, care for, and support one another.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of a family in their own words.
Step 3: Types of Family - The teacher explains the two main types of family:
- Nuclear family - Father, mother, and children.
- Extended family - Nuclear family plus grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews, nieces, and other relatives.
The teacher uses charts to illustrate both family types.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify whether each chart shows a nuclear or an extended family.
Step 4: Members of Nuclear and Extended Family - The teacher discusses the members of each type of family and explains their relationships. The teacher also introduces a simple family tree to help pupils understand family relationships.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify different family members and state their relationships using the family tree.
Step 5: Importance of the Family - The teacher explains the importance of the family, including:
- Providing love and care.
- Providing food, clothing, and shelter.
- Protecting family members.
- Teaching good morals and discipline.
- Supporting children’s education.
- Promoting unity and cooperation.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways their families help and support them.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of a family.
- Group 2: Differentiate between a nuclear family and an extended family.
- Group 3: Draw and label a simple family tree showing members of a nuclear and extended family.
- Group 4: State the importance of the family and present examples from everyday life.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, draw, identify, and present their assigned tasks.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meaning of family, the types of family, the members of nuclear and extended families, and the importance of the family.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and assesses pupils’ ability to identify family members and distinguish between nuclear and extended families.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions, identify family members correctly, and explain the importance of the family.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

2. Meaning, Types and Elements of Culture
3. Major Cultures in Nigeria
4. Importance of Culture
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of culture.
2. Identify the two main types of culture.
3. Differentiate between material and non-material culture.
4. Mention at least six elements of culture.
5. Identify some major cultural groups in Nigeria.
6. Give examples of cultural practices among the Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa-Fulani.

This lesson builds on that knowledge because marriage ceremonies, family relationships, greetings, clothing, food, festivals, and traditional practices are all parts of culture.

In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning and types of culture, the elements of culture, and some of the major cultures in Nigeria, including the Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa-Fulani cultures.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF CULTURE
Culture is the way of life of a group of people. It includes the things they believe, do, speak, eat, wear, and practise.
Culture is learned from parents, family members, elders, and the community and is passed from one generation to another.
TYPES OF CULTURE
1. Material Culture
Material culture refers to the physical things made or used by people as part of their way of life.
Examples include:
- Traditional clothes
- Houses
- Tools
- Musical instruments
- Jewellery
- Food
- Artwork
2. Non-Material Culture
Non-material culture refers to the ideas, beliefs, values, customs, and practices of a people.
Examples include:
- Language
- Religion
- Beliefs
- Customs
- Traditions
- Moral values
- Greetings
ELEMENTS OF CULTURE
Some important elements of culture include:
1. Language - The means people use to communicate with one another.
2. Food - The types of food people prepare and eat.
3. Clothing - The types of clothes people wear.
4. Religion and beliefs - What people believe about God, life, and spiritual matters.
5. Music and dance - Songs, rhythms, and dances associated with a people.
6. Customs and traditions - Accepted ways of behaving and doing things.
7. Festivals - Special occasions celebrated by people.
8. Arts and crafts - Creative works made by people.
9. Greetings - Ways people show respect when meeting one another.
10. Values - Ideas about what is considered good, right, and important.
LESSON 2 - MAJOR CULTURES IN NIGERIA
Nigeria is a culturally diverse country with many ethnic groups. Some of the major cultural groups include:
1. Yoruba Culture
The Yoruba people are mainly found in southwestern Nigeria.
Examples of Yoruba cultural practices include:
- Yoruba language
- Traditional clothing such as Aso-Oke
- Traditional music and dance
- Festivals such as Osun-Osogbo
- Respect for elders
- Traditional foods such as amala and ewedu
2. Igbo Culture
The Igbo people are mainly found in southeastern Nigeria.
Examples include:
- Igbo language
- Traditional clothing
- Igbo music and dances
- New Yam Festival
- Respect for elders
- Traditional foods such as yam, fufu, and soups
3. Hausa-Fulani Culture
The Hausa-Fulani people are mainly found in northern Nigeria.
Examples include:
- Hausa language
- Traditional clothing such as babban riga
- Traditional music and dances
- Durbar festival
- Islamic traditions
- Foods such as tuwo and various soups
IMPORTANCE OF CULTURE
Culture is important because it:
1. Gives people a sense of identity.
2. Preserves the history of a people.
3. Promotes unity and a sense of belonging.
4. Teaches good values and acceptable behaviour.
5. Helps people respect their heritage.
6. Promotes Nigerian cultural diversity.
7. Provides opportunities for tourism and cultural activities.

They learned that there are two main types of culture:

CULTURE: CULTURAL DIFFERENCES, EXTERNAL INFLUENCES AND SIMILARITIES AMONG NIGERIAN CULTURES
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 4
THEME - OUR CULTURE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Our Culture: Meaning and Types of Culture, Elements of Culture and Major Cultures in Nigeria | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 5 Social Studies
TOPIC - CULTURAL DIFFERENCES AND SIMILARITIES
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Examples of Cultural Differences in Nigeria
3. External Influences on Culture and Similarities Among Nigerian Cultures
4. Importance of Respecting Cultural Differences
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of cultural differences.
2. Identify some cultural differences among Nigerians.
3. Mention the external influences on culture.
4. State the positive and negative effects of external influences on culture.
5. Identify some similarities among Nigerian cultures.
6. Explain the importance of respecting cultural differences.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned the meaning and types of culture, the elements of culture, and the major cultural groups in Nigeria.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by helping pupils understand the differences and similarities among Nigerian cultures and how outside influences can affect culture.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of people from different Nigerian cultural groups
2. Pictures of traditional clothing, foods, festivals, and greetings
3. Charts showing cultural differences and similarities
4. Flashcards

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Pupils have seen that people in different parts of Nigeria speak different languages, wear different clothes, eat different foods, and celebrate different festivals. Even though these cultures are different, Nigerians also share many good values, such as respecting elders, loving their families, and welcoming visitors. Some cultural practices have changed because of education, religion, technology, and contact with other people.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about cultural differences, external influences on culture, and the similarities among Nigerian cultures.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF CULTURAL DIFFERENCES
Cultural differences are the ways in which the culture of one group of people is different from that of another group.
People may differ in their:
1. Language - The way people speak and communicate with one another.
2. Dressing - The type of clothes people wear.
3. Food - The kinds of meals people prepare and eat.
4. Greetings - The way people welcome or show respect to one another.
5. Music and dance - The songs and dances people perform during celebrations and other occasions.
6. Festivals - Special events or celebrations observed by a community or cultural group.
7. Customs and traditions - The accepted ways of behaving and doing things that are passed from one generation to another.
EXAMPLES OF CULTURAL DIFFERENCES IN NIGERIA
1. The Yoruba mainly speak the Yoruba language, while the Igbo speak Igbo and the Hausa-Fulani speak Hausa.
2. Different cultural groups wear different traditional clothes.
3. People prepare and eat different traditional foods.
4. Greetings may be different from one culture to another.
5. Festivals and traditional dances vary among different cultural groups.
LESSON 2 - EXTERNAL INFLUENCES ON CULTURE
External influences are things from outside that can affect or change the culture of a people.
Examples include:
1. Education - Learning new knowledge and skills in school or from other people.
2. Religion - The way people worship God and practise their faith.
3. Technology - The use of machines, computers, phones, and other tools to make work easier.
4. Television and movies - Programmes and films that people watch for learning and entertainment.
5. Internet and social media - Online platforms people use to get information and communicate with others.
6. Trade and business - Buying, selling, and exchanging goods and services.
7. Travelling - Moving from one place to another to visit, learn, or do business.
8. Interaction with people from other cultures - Meeting, talking to, and learning from people who have different ways of life.
POSITIVE EXTERNAL INFLUENCES
1. Learning new ideas
2. Better education
3. Improved communication
4. Better healthcare
5. Peaceful relationship with other cultures
NEGATIVE EXTERNAL INFLUENCES
1. Loss of traditional languages
2. Loss of traditional dressing
3. Forgetting traditional customs
4. Copying harmful behaviours
5. Reduced interest in cultural festivals
LESSON 3 - SIMILARITIES AMONG NIGERIAN CULTURES
Although Nigerians have different cultures, they also share many similarities.
These include:
1. Respect for elders - Showing honour, obedience, and good manners to older people.
2. Love for family - Caring for, helping, and supporting members of the family.
3. Marriage ceremonies - Special events where a man and a woman are joined together as husband and wife.
4. Naming ceremonies - Special occasions held to give a name to a newborn baby.
5. Traditional music and dance - Songs and dances performed according to the customs of a people.
6. Hospitality to visitors - Welcoming and treating visitors kindly.
7. Community cooperation - People working together to help and develop their community.
8. Celebration of festivals - Coming together to observe special cultural or traditional events.
IMPORTANCE OF RESPECTING CULTURAL DIFFERENCES
Respecting cultural differences helps to:
1. Promote peace and unity.
2. Encourage understanding among different people.
3. Preserve Nigerian cultural heritage.
4. Reduce discrimination.
5. Promote national unity.
6. Encourage peaceful coexistence.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions

A. games
B. numbers
C. colours
D. languages

7. Computers, phones, and the Internet are part of ______.

10. People celebrate traditional ______ at special times.
C. True or False
11. All Nigerians speak the same language. ______
12. Education can influence culture. ______
13. Respect for elders is not common in many Nigerian cultures. ______
14. Travelling can help people learn about other cultures. ______
15. We should respect the cultures of other people. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Language - A. Welcoming people kindly
17. Dressing - B. The clothes people wear
18. Hospitality - C. The way people communicate
19. Technology - D. Phones and computers
20. Festivals - E. Special cultural celebrations
ANSWER KEYS

6. language

8. visitors
9. family
10. festivals
11. False
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. C 17. B 18. A 19. D 20. E
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that cultural differences are the ways in which the culture of one group of people is different from that of another. These differences may be seen in language, dressing, food, greetings, music and dance, festivals, and customs.
Pupils also learned that external influences such as education, religion, technology, television, the Internet, trade, travelling, and interaction with people from other cultures can affect culture in both positive and negative ways.
Finally, pupils learned that although Nigerian cultures are different, they share many similarities such as respect for elders, love for family, hospitality, community cooperation, marriage ceremonies, naming ceremonies, traditional music and dance, and the celebration of festivals. Respecting cultural differences helps to promote peace, unity, and national development.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of Nigerians from different cultural groups wearing different traditional clothes, eating different foods, speaking different languages, and celebrating festivals.
The teacher asks:
- What differences do you notice in these pictures?
- What things are the same?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and identify differences and similarities.
Step 2: Meaning of Cultural Differences
The teacher explains that cultural differences are the ways in which the culture of one group of people is different from that of another.
Examples include differences in:
- Language
- Dressing
- Food
- Greetings
- Music and dance
- Festivals
- Customs and traditions
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention examples of cultural differences they know.
Step 3: External Influences on Culture
The teacher explains that external influences are things from outside that can affect or change culture.
Examples include:
- Education

- Technology
- Television and movies

- Trade and business

The teacher explains the positive and negative effects of these influences.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify ways technology and education have changed some cultural practices.
Step 4: Similarities Among Nigerian Cultures

Examples include:

- Traditional music and dance
- Hospitality to visitors

- Celebration of festivals
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention similarities they have observed in different Nigerian cultures.
Step 5: Importance of Respecting Cultural Differences

- Promote peace.
- Promote unity.
- Encourage understanding.
- Reduce discrimination.
- Preserve Nigerian cultural heritage.
- Promote national development.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss why they should respect people from other cultural groups.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into three groups.
- Group 1: List five cultural differences among Nigerians.
- Group 2: List five external influences on culture.
- Group 3: List five similarities among Nigerian cultures.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their work.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of cultural differences, external influences on culture, and the similarities among Nigerian cultures.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation

THEME - OUR CULTURE

LEARNING

LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of cultural preservation.
2. List ways of preserving culture.
3. Identify some harmful cultural practices that should be discarded.
4. Mention the good cultural values that should be preserved.
5. Explain the importance of preserving good culture.
7. Show willingness to respect and promote positive cultural values.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about culture, cultural differences, external influences on culture, and similarities among Nigerian cultures.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils how to preserve culture, avoid harmful cultural practices, and promote good cultural values.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of Nigerian cultural festivals
2. Pictures of traditional clothing, music, dance, and arts
3. Charts showing good cultural values

METHOD OF TEACHING

Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Pupils have seen people wear traditional clothes, speak their local languages, celebrate festivals, greet elders respectfully, and perform traditional music and dances. These cultural practices help to preserve our heritage. However, some old practices are harmful and should no longer be encouraged.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of cultural preservation, ways of preserving culture, harmful cultural practices to discard, and good cultural values that should be preserved.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF CULTURAL PRESERVATION
Cultural preservation means protecting, respecting, and passing our culture from one generation to another so that it is not forgotten.
WAYS OF PRESERVING CULTURE
We can preserve our culture by:
1. Speaking our local languages.
2. Wearing traditional clothes during cultural occasions.
3. Teaching children about their culture.
4. Respecting cultural values and traditions.
5. Celebrating cultural festivals.
6. Learning traditional music and dance.
7. Preserving traditional arts and crafts.
8. Reading books and stories about Nigerian cultures.
9. Visiting museums and cultural centres.
10. Showing respect for elders and community leaders.
LESSON 2 - HARMFUL CULTURAL PRACTICES TO DISCARD
Some cultural practices are harmful and should not be continued.
Examples include:
1. Child marriage - Marrying a boy or girl before he or she is old enough to marry.
2. Female genital mutilation (FGM) - A harmful practice in which part of a girl’s private body is cut. It can cause pain and health problems.
3. Discrimination against people - Treating some people unfairly because they are different.
4. Treating people unfairly because of gender or disability - Not giving people equal treatment because they are male or female, or because they have a disability.
5. Harmful traditional rituals - Traditional practices that can hurt or endanger people.
6. Violence in the name of culture - Hurting or fighting people and claiming it is part of culture.
7. Denying children the right to education - Preventing children from going to school and learning.
These practices should be rejected because they can harm people and violate their rights.
LESSON 3 - GOOD CULTURAL VALUES TO PRESERVE
Some good cultural values should be encouraged and preserved.
Examples include:
1. Respect for elders - Showing honour, obedience, and good manners to older people.
2. Honesty - Always telling the truth and not cheating or stealing.
3. Hard work - Doing your work carefully and not being lazy.
4. Hospitality - Welcoming visitors and treating them kindly.
5. Love and kindness - Caring for others and treating them with compassion.
6. Unity - Living and working together peacefully.
7. Cooperation - Helping one another to achieve a common goal.
8. Peaceful living - Living happily without fighting or causing trouble.
9. Respect for one another - Treating everyone politely and valuing their feelings and rights.
10. Good manners - Behaving politely by saying “please,” “thank you,” greeting others, and showing respect.
IMPORTANCE OF PRESERVING GOOD CULTURE
Preserving good culture helps to:
1. Protect our cultural heritage.
2. Teach good behaviour.
3. Promote unity.
4. Strengthen family and community relationships.
5. Build national pride.
6. Encourage peace among people.
7. Preserve Nigerian traditions for future generations.

INTRODUCTION

In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of religion, the types of religion practised in Nigeria, and the materials used for worship in different religions.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF RELIGION
Religion is the belief in and worship of God or a supreme being. It teaches people how to live good lives, love others, and obey God’s commandments.
TYPES OF RELIGION IN NIGERIA
The three main types of religion practised in Nigeria are:
1. Christianity
Christianity is the religion of people who believe in Jesus Christ as the Son of God and Saviour.
Christians worship in a church.
2. Islam
Islam is the religion of people who believe in Allah and follow the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him).
Muslims worship in a mosque.
3. African Traditional Religion (ATR)
African Traditional Religion is the indigenous religion practised by some African communities before Christianity and Islam became widespread.
Followers worship according to their traditional beliefs and customs.

2. Singing hymns or religious songs

4. Attending places of worship

LESSON 1 - MEANING OF BELIEFS
Beliefs are the ideas or things that people accept as true, especially about God, religion, and life.
RESPECTING OTHER PEOPLE’S RELIGIOUS BELIEFS
People belong to different religions and have different beliefs. We should respect everyone’s religious beliefs even if they are different from ours.
Ways of showing respect include:
1. Being polite to everyone.
2. Allowing others to worship peacefully.
3. Avoiding insults about another person’s religion.
4. Listening respectfully to others.
5. Living peacefully with people of different religions.

LESSON 2 - MEANING OF TRADITIONS
Traditions are customs, practices, and ways of life that are passed from one generation to another.
RESPECTING OTHER PEOPLE’S TRADITIONS

1. Appreciating their culture.
2. Avoiding discrimination.
3. Joining peaceful cultural celebrations when invited.
4. Respecting traditional leaders and elders.
5. Learning about other cultures.

- Praying
- Reading the Bible
- Singing hymns
- Attending church services
- Giving offerings

- Praying to Allah

- Respecting traditional customs

SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that beliefs are the ideas people accept as true, while traditions are customs and practices passed from one generation to another. They learned that people have different religious beliefs, traditions, and methods of worship, and that everyone deserves respect.
Pupils also learned different ways of showing respect for other people’s beliefs and traditions, such as being polite, allowing others to worship peacefully, avoiding discrimination, listening respectfully, and living peacefully with everyone.
Finally, they learned that respecting other people’s beliefs and traditions promotes peace, unity, tolerance, friendship, and peaceful coexistence in the family, school, community, and nation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of people from different religions worshipping in a church, mosque, and traditional place of worship.
The teacher asks:
- What are the people doing?
- Do all people worship in the same way?
- How should we treat people whose beliefs are different from ours?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Beliefs
The teacher explains:
- Beliefs are the ideas people accept as true, especially about God and religion.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of beliefs in their own words.
Step 3: Respecting Other People’s Religious Beliefs
The teacher explains that people belong to different religions and should respect one another.
Ways of showing respect include:
- Being polite to everyone.
- Allowing others to worship peacefully.
- Avoiding insults about another person’s religion.
- Listening respectfully to others.
- Living peacefully with people of different religions.
- Showing kindness to everyone.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss how they can respect people of different religions.
Step 4: Meaning of Traditions
The teacher explains:
- Traditions are customs and practices passed from one generation to another.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of traditions in their own words.
Step 5: Respecting Other People’s Traditions
The teacher explains that people also have different traditions which should be respected.
Ways of showing respect include:
- Appreciating other cultures.
- Avoiding discrimination.
- Joining peaceful cultural celebrations when invited.
- Respecting traditional leaders and elders.
- Learning about other cultures.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention traditions they know and explain how to respect them.
Step 6: Methods of Worship in Nigeria
The teacher explains that different religions worship in different ways.
Christianity
- Pray
- Read the Bible
- Sing hymns
- Attend church services
Islam
- Pray to Allah
- Read the Qur’an
- Observe daily prayers
- Fast during Ramadan
African Traditional Religion
- Offer traditional prayers
- Perform traditional ceremonies
- Respect traditional customs
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the different methods of worship.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: List five ways of respecting other people’s religious beliefs.
- Group 2: List five ways of respecting other people’s traditions.
- Group 3: Compare the methods of worship in Christianity, Islam, and African Traditional Religion.
- Group 4: Explain five benefits of respecting people of different beliefs and traditions.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their work.
Step 8: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of beliefs and traditions, ways of respecting other people’s beliefs and traditions, and the methods of worship in Nigeria.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 9: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise to assess their understanding.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the multiple choice, fill-in-the-gaps, true or false, and matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
